turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, good to meet you. I, uh... I guess I'm just having some trouble on the job lately. Driving. 

Over the last few months, my mind just... keeps jumping around. Every little CB chirp, or a fuel price sign, or just some new idea pops in my head... I get sidetracked. I'm starting to miss details I normally never miss. Like, uh, a client's delivery note, or forgetting who I promised I'd call back. 

So... yeah. That's what finally got me in here.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly states they are starting to miss details they normally never miss, such as a client's delivery note.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes getting easily sidetracked by extraneous stimuli like CB chirps and fuel price signs.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient mentions forgetting daily activities, specifically forgetting who they promised to call back.
symptom_reasoning.S039: The patient reports their mind keeps jumping around and is easily drawn to irrelevant external stimuli and new ideas.

turns.patient_response: Yeah, I suppose so. Most nights lately I only sleep maybe... three or four hours. But I'm up before daylight. I don't feel worn out or anything, though. Just... ready to roll. That's about it.

symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient agrees to feeling unusually energized and describes waking up 'ready to roll'.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly states they only sleep three or four hours a night but do not feel worn out.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually upbeat or euphoric lately?
turns.patient_response:
Euphoric... I don't know about that word. But, uh... I guess I've been pretty fired up for a few months now. Just feeling like everything's gonna work out fine, no matter what. 

But then I also get, well... I've been snapping over small stuff at home. Out in the yard and whatnot. It ain't really my usual way to be like that. So... yeah.

symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient reports 'snapping over small stuff,' indicating a state of reacting sharply to minor stimuli.

symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient confirms taking on extra jobs and activities like rewriting route plans and fixing things around the house.

turns.doctor_question: When you only sleep three or four hours, do you still feel fully rested?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I guess so. Most nights I'm only getting about three, maybe four hours. But... I wake up before the sun's even up, and I ain't tired. Just... ready to get going. Don't feel worn out at all.

turns.doctor_question: Do your thoughts ever feel like they’re going too fast for you to keep up with?
turns.patient_response: No... can't say they do. My head's just... doing its regular thing, I guess. I just focus on what I gotta get done for the day, or the road ahead of me. They ain't going too fast or anything like that.

symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient explicitly denies that their thoughts are going too fast, stating their head is doing its regular thing.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been drinking more alcohol lately?
turns.patient_response: No... not really. I mean, I drive for a living, so... I can't really be doing that. Just the usual, if I have anything at all. Nothing more than normal.

turns.doctor_question: Have these changes started causing serious problems at work or at home?
turns.patient_response: Well... I guess you could say things have been a bit bumpy. Work's... well, I've had to ask dispatch to repeat themselves a few times lately. Lost track of some details I usually wouldn't. And a couple of sales calls just... slipped my mind. I was just thinking about too many other things, I guess. And at home... my wife and daughter, they've been kinda quiet around me. Like they're being careful. I know I'm probably not helping things there right now.

symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient mentions having to ask dispatch to repeat themselves, indicating difficulty listening or processing when spoken to.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient notes he was 'thinking about too many other things,' which aligns with distractibility from unrelated thoughts.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient admits that a couple of sales calls 'slipped my mind,' demonstrating forgetfulness in daily work activities.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been using any stimulants, like methamphetamine, cocaine, or prescription ADHD pills?
turns.patient_response: No. I don't touch any of that stuff. Never have. Like I said, I drive a truck. Can't be messing around with things like that.

turns.doctor_question: Before these past few months, have you ever had another time in your life when you only needed a few hours of sleep and still felt fully rested?
turns.patient_response: No, I... I don't think so. Usually, I'm a guy who needs his solid eight hours. This... not needing sleep thing, it's just been lately. Never really had that happen before.

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient confirms currently experiencing a 'not needing sleep thing' lately, indicating a decreased need for sleep.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to notice?

turns.doctor_question: Lately, have you felt more confident or capable than usual?
turns.patient_response: I guess so. I mean... I had this idea lately. I figured I could just... rebuild the whole driver training program for the company. Do it all myself. Thought I could make it run a lot better than the bosses ever could. Which, you know... I just drive. It's not really my lane to be doing all that. But I just felt like I could do it no problem.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient describes an inflated sense of capability and grandiosity, believing they could single-handedly rebuild the company's training program better than management despite it not being their job.

turns.doctor_question: During these past few months, have you also had stretches where you felt down or depressed most of the day?
turns.patient_response: No. I... I wouldn't say that. I haven't really felt down or anything. Just... been going about my business, mostly.

turns.doctor_question: Before all this started, did you have a head injury?
turns.patient_response: No. I haven't... no head injuries. Nothing like that.

turns.doctor_question: Before these changes started, were you diagnosed with any new medical condition?

turns.doctor_question: Have these changes gotten so severe that you’ve been unable to do your job or carry out your usual responsibilities?
turns.patient_response:
I wouldn't say unable. I'm still doing my job. Just... maybe slipped up a little bit. I've had to ask dispatch and a few clients to repeat details I normally keep track of. Dropped the ball on a couple of sales follow-ups because I was... just chasing too many ideas at once, I guess. 

And at home, it's... well, my wife and daughter are kind of walking on eggshells. I can tell I'm adding strain there when I should be helping. But I'm still working.
